newsitem.title: USA: Ben & Jerry's looks to Phish for profits.
newsitem.headline: Ben & Jerry's looks to Phish for profits.

text.p: Ben & Jerry's Homemade Inc said it hopes Phish, a new chocolate flavored ice cream with marshmallow and caramel that it started shipping in March, will help its operations return to profitability this year.

"We're optimistic for Phish. It's been very much a big hit," Chief Financial Officer Frances Rathke said of the flavor named after a rock band that plays its own material in the style of the Grateful Dead.
Earlier, the South Burlington, Vermont premium ice cream maker said it expects a net loss on slower sales in the first quarter.
"This is a first for us," Rathke said of the company's expected first quarter loss which is anticipated to be in the $.12 to $.15 per share range.

She said 20 percent of the sales volume decline during the latest quarter occured in the midwest amid flooding that was so bad "our trucks couldn't get to the stores or even our customers could not literally make it to the stores."
She said profit margins also suffered from continuing high diary costs, a "pretty flat industry" and reduced production levels.

Edward Froelich who follows Ben & Jerry's for Pershing, a division of DLJ, said of the company's report of a loss, "there's not a positive glow on this. They're looking for Phish to do well, but we can't be enthusiatic at this point."
"It's trading near its low for the year and could set a new one," Froelich said. "It is something that has value, but that's not shining through today."

Ben & Jerry's reported a decrease in net sales in the first quarter of approximately five to seven percent as compared to the same period a year earlier. Those disappointing sales, along wtih planned reduced production levels to lower the company's inventories, "significantly reduced the company's gross margins in the first quarter of 1997," Ben & Jerry's said in a statement.
The company said it anticipates a return to profitablity for the remaining quarters.
